prompt: The graph of $y = \sin(x - 30^\circ)$ is the graph of $y = \sin(x)$ slid sideways. How many degrees does it slide to the RIGHT?
hint: A phase shift slides the whole wave sideways. Look at the number subtracted inside the brackets.

hints.text: A phase shift slides the whole wave sideways. Look at the number subtracted inside the brackets.
In $y = \sin(x - c)$, the wave slides $c$ degrees to the RIGHT. Here $c = 30$.

explanation: For $\sin(x - 30^\circ)$, the inside is zero when $x = 30^\circ$, so the wave starts its climb $30^\circ$ later.
Starting later means the whole wave has slid $30^\circ$ to the RIGHT.

alternativeExplanations.title: Ask when the inside is zero
steps: Whatever plain sine did at 0, the shifted wave does when the inside equals 0.
x − 30 = 0 gives x = 30. Every feature arrives 30° later, which is a slide right.

alternativeExplanations.title: The late-running tide
steps: Think of high tide arriving 30 minutes later than usual each day.
The tide pattern is exactly the same shape, just running late. Running late = sliding right on a time graph.
